subject: Social Habits
title: Respect for people
objectives: Children will greet and speak kindly to elders and helpers.
Children will accept that people are different and treat them kindly.
content: Respecting elders and teachers, respecting helpers, and respecting different people.
teachingActivities: Respect is shown in many ways across Nigerian homes (greeting, kneeling or bowing, using titles, listening); teach respect as kindness and listening, accept each family’s way, and never require a child to perform a gesture that their family does not use; use dolls and puppets to show respect for people who look, speak or move differently.
learnerActivities: Greet and speak kindly to elders and helpers and treat people who are different from us with kindness.
resources: Pictures of elders, teachers, cleaners, drivers and gatekeepers
assessment: Observe whether each child greets elders and helpers and uses kind words with a child who is different.
expectedOutcomes: Greets an elder or helper in a family-appropriate way.
Uses kind words with a child who looks different.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: people around us

lessons.title: Respecting elders and teachers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will greet elders and teachers respectfully in a way their family uses.
successCriteria: Greets an elder with words or a gesture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use manners, tell the truth and care for belongings.
lessons.starter: Show a puppet grandparent and say "Good morning, Grandma." Let the puppet answer warmly.
teacherActivities: Show pictures of elders and teachers and say who they are.
Show how to greet with a smile and good morning.
Ask children how they greet elders at home.
Say "We listen and speak kindly to elders."
learnerActivities: Child shows or says their greeting if they wish.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of elders and teachers and say who they are. Children: Children look and name them.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to greet with a smile and good morning. Children: Children greet the puppet.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask children how they greet elders at home. Children: Child shows or says their greeting if they wish.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We listen and speak kindly to elders." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Greeting elders
steps: Show how you greet at home.
practical.safety: Accept every family’s way of greeting and never require a particular gesture. Keep puppet play gentle.

differentiation.support: Greet together and use a simple word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend a greeting from home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with a respectful greeting.
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child how your family greets elders.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "greet elders and teachers respectfully in a way their family uses" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Good morning, Grandma, good morning, Grandpa.

lessons.title: Respecting helpers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will greet and thank people who help the school.
successCriteria: Says thank you to a helper
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use manners, tell the truth and care for belongings.
resources: Pictures of the cleaner, gatekeeper, cook, driver and nurse
lessons.starter: Show a picture of the school cleaner and say "This person keeps our school clean. We say thank you."
teacherActivities: Show each helper picture and say what they do.
Say "We greet helpers and say thank you."
Walk to meet a helper and let children greet them.
learnerActivities: Children look and repeat the job.
Children say hello and thank you.
Child makes a mark on the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each helper picture and say what they do. Children: Children look and repeat the job.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "We greet helpers and say thank you." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk to meet a helper and let children greet them. Children: Children say hello and thank you.
Step 4. Teacher: Make a thank-you card together. Children: Child makes a mark on the card.

practical.title: Thank our helpers
practical.safety: Keep the walk short and supervised and ask the helper beforehand. Use non-toxic crayons.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and greet together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what a helper does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say to helpers?

lessons.conclusion: Give the thank-you card and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Greet and thank helpers you meet with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "greet and thank people who help the school" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Everyone is different
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will notice that people are different and treat everyone kindly.
successCriteria: Uses kind words to a child who is different
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use manners, tell the truth and care for belongings.
resources: Dolls or pictures of children of different skin tones, abilities and clothing
lessons.starter: Show two dolls that look different and say "These friends look different. They are both our friends."
teacherActivities: Show pictures of children who look and move differently.
Look in a mirror and say "I am special."
Play a game where friends do different things.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of children who look and move differently. Children: Children look and say friend.
Step 2. Teacher: Look in a mirror and say "I am special." Children: Child looks and smiles.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "We are kind to everyone." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Play a game where friends do different things. Children: Child plays with a friend.

practical.title: We are all friends
practical.safety: Answer children’s questions about differences simply and kindly and never allow teasing. Use an unbreakable mirror.

differentiation.support: Look at the picture together and say friend.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say one way they are like a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "We are friends."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk kindly about differences when your child notices them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice that people are different and treat everyone kindly" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Respect role play
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will act out respectful greetings and thanks in role play.
successCriteria: Uses thank you in role play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use manners, tell the truth and care for belongings.
resources: Hats for a teacher, a nurse and a driver
lessons.starter: Show three hats and say "Today we meet three helpers. Let us greet them."
teacherActivities: Put on a hat and say "I am the nurse."
Let each child try a hat and be the helper.
Swap roles so everyone has a go.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put on a hat and say "I am the nurse." Children: Children greet the nurse.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child try a hat and be the helper. Children: Child takes a role.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Thank you for helping us." Children: Children say thank you.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles so everyone has a go. Children: Child swaps and plays again.

practical.title: Helper role play
practical.safety: Use hats that are clean and shared fairly and supervise swapping. Keep play gentle.

differentiation.support: Play the helper with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the helper and greet them.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says thank you in role play
lessons.conclusion: Take off the hats and say "Thank you, helpers."
lessons.homeConnection: Play helpers at home and practise greetings.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out respectful greetings and thanks in role play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 respect check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child shows respect.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can use manners, tell the truth and care for belongings.
lessons.starter: Sing the respect song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: elders, helpers and different friends.
At each station watch how the child behaves.
learnerActivities: Child responds with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: elders, helpers and different friends. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child behaves. Children: Child responds with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Respect stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep play gentle. Respect every family’s way of showing respect.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to greet a visitor.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: greets an elder; thanks a helper; is kind to a child who is different; listens to adults.

questions.question: What do we say to an elder?
What do we say to helpers?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep showing respect to everyone at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child shows respect" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
